examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Blocked threats rose 12.4 percent. A rise in threats is bad, so the tile sets inverse and the delta reads as a regression.

examples.name: Deltas
examples.summary: A good rise, a bad rise with inverse, a flat change, and no delta at all.

examples.name: Variants
examples.summary: variant="mono" (default) draws the big-number mono figure of a usage strip; variant="sans" draws the large heading figure of a traffic summary. The unit is always smaller, muted and sans.

examples.name: CountUp
examples.summary: Press Refresh to count the figure up from its previous value. Timer driven, so it is excluded from visual regression; Default is its static sibling. Reduced motion renders the final value at once.

examples.name: Loading
examples.summary: A Skeleton line holds the place of the figure and the delta.

examples.name: Empty
examples.summary: No value for the range: a dash, announced as No value, over a muted placeholder line marked No data. Leave out the delta and the trend rather than showing a zero.

examples.name: Markdown
examples.summary: The same data written in a docs page: `DocMarkdown` turns a `<StatTile value={48210} />` tag into a real `StatTile`. The attribute values are JSON, so a docs author copies them from the props or a page entry and never imports the component.

examples.name: Page JSON
examples.summary: The same data in the marketing site's page JSON: `StatTile` is a scene, so a band places it by name in its `scene` slot (here `console-showcase-section` with `variant: "diagram"`) and `SitePage` renders the entry with no code.
